deep.reconstruction:
This page is printed text in Fraktur type, not Gauss's handwriting. It is from a German arithmetic and algebra textbook bound into the bundle; the shelfmark suggests Christian Leiste's 'Arithmetik und Algebra'. The page itself carries no handwritten notes. The facing page 78 has handwritten columns of numbers in the margin; on the transcription they look like primes between about 9700 and 9973, consistent with Gauss's prime-counting tables.

Setting: a capital a earns interest at rate b/c per year. Write q = (c+b)/c. The numerical values come from §163 and are confirmed on p.78: b=1, c=25 (so 4%), ab=5000 (a=5000), n=10.

(§165, conclusion) Each year an extra amount d is added. After n years the capital has grown to q^n·a, and to this one must add the sum of a geometric series with first term d, ratio q and n terms. By §155 that sum is d(q^n−1)/(q−1). Since q−1 = b/c, this equals (q^n·c − c)d/b. Total: S = q^n·a + cd(q^n−1)/b = q^n·(ab+cd)/b − cd/b.

Example with d=100: n·log q = 10·log(26/25) = 0.170333, and log(ab+cd) = log 7500 = 3.8750613. Adding gives 4.0453943 = log 11101.8. Here b=1, so the division by b is tacit. Subtract cd = 2500: S = 8601.8 Reichsthaler.

(§166, corollary) If instead d is withdrawn every year, the geometric sum is subtracted: S = q^n·a − cd(q^n−1)/b = [q^n(ab−cd) + cd]/b.

(§167) Find the n at which the capital is fully consumed. Setting S=0 requires cd > ab, since otherwise every term is positive. Write ab−cd = −(cd−ab). Then −q^n(cd−ab) + cd = 0, so q^n = cd/(cd−ab), n·log q = log(cd/(cd−ab)), and n = log(cd/(cd−ab)) / log q.

The example follows on p.78: d=500 gives q^n = 12500/7500 = 5/3, so n = 0.2218487/0.0170333 ≈ 13.02 years.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.
In the numerical example the final division by b is omitted without comment; this is harmless because b=1.
The page gives log(26/25)·10 as 0.170333 (seven-place logs truncated to six places); this is fine. On p.78 the per-year value 0.0170333 is consistent with it.

results.what: Accumulated value of a capital with annual deposits: q^n·a + d(q^n−1)/(q−1) = q^n(ab+cd)/b − cd/b
results.modern_name: Future value of a principal plus an ordinary annuity (compound interest)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard commercial and political arithmetic of the 17th–18th centuries (e.g., Leibniz, de Witt, Euler textbooks)

results.what: Value after n years with annual withdrawals: [q^n(ab−cd)+cd]/b
Term until exhaustion: n = log(cd/(cd−ab)) / log((c+b)/c), valid only if cd > ab
results.modern_name: Number of periods of an annuity that exhausts a loan or capital (logarithmic solution)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed page of a standard 18th-century arithmetic textbook on compound interest and annuities. It contains no Gauss handwriting and nothing beyond routine material.

checkable.asserts: The closed form for capital plus deposits; the expression simplifies to 0.
The withdrawal formula of §166; the expression simplifies to 0.
Equals about 13.02 years, the §167 example on p.78.

transcription_corrections: The page is printed Fraktur type, not a Gauss manuscript; there are no handwritten annotations on this page.
The §155 formula should read ((q^n − 1)·d)/(q − 1) with q=(c+b)/c; the transcription renders this correctly.
'Größe des Capitals mit Zinsen und Zulage ist 8601, 8 rthl.' means 8601.8 rthl (the comma is a decimal separator).
